source_text: Nec quisquam miretur, dilectissimi fratres, etiam de confessoribus quosdam ad ista procedere, inde quoque aliquos tam nefanda, tam grauia peccare. neque enim confessio inmunem facit ab insidiis diaboli aut contra temptationes et pericula et incursus adque impetus saeculares adhuc in saeculo positum perpetua securitate defendit: ceterum numquam in confessoribus fraudes et stupra et adulteria postmodum uideremus quae nunc in quibusdam uidentes ingemescimus et dolemus. quisque ille confessor est Salomone maior aut melior aut Deo carior non est: qui tamen quamdiu in uiis Domini ambulauit, tamdiu gratiam quam de Domino fuerat consecutus obtinuit, postquam dereliquit Domini uiam, perdidit et gratiam Domini. et ideo scriptum est: tene quod habes, ne alius accipiat coronam tuam. quod utique Dominus non minaretur auferri posse coronam iustitiae, nisi quia recedente iustitia recedat necesse est et corona.
thought_title: Confessors are not safe from sin
orientation: Cyprian is addressing the faithful about the danger of schism, and now turns to the fact that even confessors can fall into grave sins.
pass_a_gloss: And let no one wonder, most beloved brothers, that even from the confessors certain ones proceed to these things, that from there also some sin such wicked, such grave things. For confession does not make one immune from the snares of the devil, nor does it defend with perpetual security against temptations and dangers and worldly attacks and assaults one still placed in the world: otherwise we would never afterward see in confessors deceits and debaucheries and adulteries, which now seeing in certain ones we groan and grieve. Whatever confessor he is, he is not greater or better than Solomon or more beloved by God: who nevertheless, as long as he walked in the ways of the Lord, so long he held the grace which he had obtained from the Lord; after he abandoned the way of the Lord, he lost also the grace of the Lord. And therefore it is written: hold what you have, lest another take your crown. Which certainly the Lord would not threaten that the crown of justice can be taken away, except because when justice departs, it is necessary that the crown also depart.

choices.why: Standard rendering of Cyprian's affectionate address to the faithful; preserves the superlative force.
Keeps the spatial metaphor of movement toward the sins just described; 'these things' refers back to schism and heresy.
Preserves the ablative of means and the adjective 'perpetua' modifying 'securitate'; emphasizes the false sense of lasting safety.
Renders each noun distinctly; 'stupra' as 'debaucheries' captures sexual immorality beyond adultery.

choices.term: gratiam quam de Domino fuerat consecutus
choices.english: the grace which he had obtained from the Lord
choices.why: Keeps the pluperfect force of 'fuerat consecutus' and the source 'de Domino'.
rejected: the grace he had received from the Lord
the favor he had gained from the Lord

choices.why: Literal rendering of the genitive; 'justice' is the quality whose departure causes the crown's loss.

bible_refs.note: tene quod habes, ne alius accipiat coronam tuam

pass_b_english: And let no one wonder, most beloved brothers, that even some of the confessors proceed to these things, and that from that group too certain people sin so wickedly and so gravely. For confession does not make a person immune from the snares of the devil, nor does it defend with perpetual security someone still placed in the world against temptations and dangers and the attacks and assaults of the age. Otherwise we would never see in confessors the deceits and debaucheries and adulteries that we now see in some and groan and grieve over. Whatever confessor he is, he is not greater or better than Solomon or more dear to God. Yet as long as Solomon walked in the ways of the Lord, so long he held the grace which he had obtained from the Lord; after he abandoned the way of the Lord, he lost also the grace of the Lord. And therefore it is written: Hold what you have, so that no one else takes your crown (Revelation 3:11). Surely the Lord would not threaten that the crown of justice could be taken away unless, when justice departs, the crown also must necessarily depart.

last_rejected.why: 'Quisque ille' means 'whoever/whatever that confessor is,' not 'whatever confessor he is' which is awkward and slightly off.
last_rejected.fix: Whoever that confessor is, he is not greater or better than Solomon or dearer to God.
last_rejected.ruling: Rendering within normal range; 'whatever confessor he is' adequately conveys quisque ille confessor est. Mere preference.
